sources.title: Forrelation: A Problem that Optimally Separates Quantum from Classical Computing
sources.edition: arXiv:1411.5729v1, 21 November 2014 (not silently the 2018 journal edition)
passages_read: Section 3.2, Proposition 6 and adjacent amplitude derivation, PDF pp. 13–14, extracted lines 659–735
Section 3.1 query conventions, pp. 12–13, bounded excerpt
Introduction k-fold discussion, located and skimmed
sources.notes: The direct k-query circuit has all-zero amplitude Phi. The controlled two-branch circuit uses ceil(k/2) queries and accepts with probability (1+Phi)/2; its stated 0.4 error convention differs from the target 1/3 convention.

sources.title: k-Forrelation Optimally Separates Quantum and Classical Query Complexity

sources.title: Quantum Amplitude Amplification and Estimation

Start of Section 2.1 through Theorem 4 and generalized phase reflections, lines 168–181

sources.title: Tight bounds on quantum searching
sources.edition: Supplied arXiv:quant-ph/9605034v1, 23 May 1996, PhysComp96 draft dated 10 May 1996; not the 1998 journal edition
passages_read: Lemmas 1–2 and Section 4 unknown number of solutions, Theorem 3 and proof, PDF pp. 3–4; extracted lines 160–300
sources.notes: Randomized Grover iteration count gives exact mean 1/2 - sin(4M theta)/(4M sin(2theta)); large-success and zero-success cases need explicit handling.

sources.title: Quantum Search on Bounded-Error Inputs
sources.edition: Supplied extracted arXiv source; online arXiv:quant-ph/0304052v2, 14 April 2003 metadata checked. The packet source tarball was not re-rendered or version-matched to the web PDF.
passages_read: Entire supplied extracted manuscript, including Sections 1–5, facts, proof, algorithm, applications, bibliography and notes
sources.notes: Robust search assumes every Fi approximates a well-defined bit fi with uniform bounded error. Arbitrary comparison probabilities lacking an underlying gap do not meet that hypothesis.

sources.title: A Quantum Algorithm for Finding the Minimum
passages_read: Entire 2-page paper: algorithm, Theorem 1, Lemmas 1–2 and final remarks
sources.notes: Threshold search relies on a genuine ordered list and uniform successful sampling. The expected analysis is converted to a bounded runtime with an explicit timeout.

Theorem 5, Claim 6 and Algorithm 2, PDF pp. 13–14 in full; Corollary 7 on p. 15

sources.title: Randomized and Quantum Query Complexities of Finding a King in a Tournament
passages_read: Section 1 technical overview of randomized and quantum algorithms, extracted lines 148–213
Section 4 complete main construction: Observation 16, Lemmas 17–18, Algorithms 2–4, Theorem 19 proof, extracted lines 529–722 and 729–766; PDF pp. 30:9–30:13
sources.notes: Appendix proofs of subroutines 17–18 not read. Exact edge oracle over a fixed tournament; history stored as W, implicit feasible set sampled uniformly. Its interface/implementation distinction is a useful writing comparison.

sources.title: Quantum Query Complexity of Tournament Solutions

sources.notes: New outside-annex primary source. Deterministic tournament edge oracle; Condorcet routine uses king finding plus verification. Lower-bound proof only beginning read. This does not establish the probabilistic-comparison theorem used by the supplied preprint.
